GROUP BY p.product_id, p.product_name

scenarios.question: For customers with order items, sum quantity multiplied by unit_price across all order statuses. Return customer_name, total_revenue and rank, highest first. Equal totals share a rank with gaps after ties.
scenarios.pseudo: I will link the relevant records by matching their customer_id values. I will link the relevant records by matching their order_id values. I will sum quantity  multiplied by  unit_price to calculate each total. I will group by customer_id and customer_name to keep one total per group. I will rank the highest total first, give equal totals the same rank, and leave gaps after ties.
scenarios.sql:
WITH customer_revenue AS (
  SELECT c.customer_id, c.customer_name, SUM(oi.quantity * oi.unit_price) AS total_revenue
  FROM customers c
  JOIN orders o ON c.customer_id = o.customer_id
  JOIN order_items oi ON o.order_id = oi.order_id
  GROUP BY c.customer_id, c.customer_name
)
SELECT customer_name, total_revenue,
       RANK() OVER (ORDER BY total_revenue DESC) AS revenue_rank
FROM customer_revenue;

       CASE

       END AS stock_status
FROM products;

);

);
